tool.name: CRISPRTarget

param.name: source
param.label: Fetch the sequences of the database from
param.help: CRISPRTarget searches the targets of the CRISPR spacers in viral, plasmid and other sequences. The public databases are distributed by the CRISPRTarget authors on Zenodo (CC-BY-4.0).
param.option: Zenodo: viral and other sequences (vhdb, ~49 MB download)

param.name: url
param.label: URL of a FASTA file
param.help: The file may be compressed with gzip or zip.

validator.message: Please enter a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL

param.name: fasta
param.label: FASTA file with the target sequences

param.name: db_id
param.label: Database identifier
param.help: A short unique identifier without whitespace, e.g. phage_2026_08. It is used as the value of the data table entry.

validator.message: The identifier must not be empty and may only contain the characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _, ., + and -

param.name: db_name
param.label: Database name
param.help: The name that is shown in the CRISPRTarget tool form, e.g. Phage (Zenodo 2026-08).

param.name: dbsize
param.label: Effective database size
param.help: Used for the BLAST statistics and for the p-values. If left empty the actual number of bases of the database is used. Give a fixed value, e.g. the 1000000000 suggested by CRISPRTarget, to obtain p-values that can be compared between databases of different sizes.

param.name: db_name
param.value: Tiny test database from a gzipped file

tool.help:
**What it does**
Builds a CRISPRTarget database from a FASTA file and adds it to the *CRISPRTarget databases* data table, so that it can be selected in the CRISPRTarget tool form.
A CRISPRTarget database consists of two parts: the *target database* with the sequences that are searched, and a *shuffled control database* with the same sequences in shuffled order. Each part is a directory with a FASTA file named after the database identifier and the corresponding BLAST database and samtools index. The latter serves as the background for the p-value calculation of the predicted targets.
The sequences can be taken from
- one of the public reference databases that are distributed by the CRISPRTarget authors on Zenodo (`viral and other sequences`_, `phage`_, `plasmid`_; CC-BY-4.0, concept DOI `10.5281/zenodo.14839268`_), - an arbitrary URL, or - a FASTA file from the history.
The database is created with *MakeUserDB.sh* and *MakeUserShuffledDB.sh* from the CRISPRTarget package, i.e. the sequence identifiers are replaced by ``SEQ_<number>|<identifier>.fa`` (the original description, which contains the accession, is kept) and a nucleotide BLAST database (``makeblastdb -parse_seqids -blastdb_version 4``) and a samtools index are created. The two directories are installed in the Galaxy data manager directory.
.. _viral and other sequences: https://zenodo.org/records/21869551/files/all_vhdb_full.fna.zip .. _phage: https://zenodo.org/records/21869551/files/phage.fa.zip .. _plasmid: https://zenodo.org/records/21869551/files/plasmid.fa.zip .. _10.5281/zenodo.14839268: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14839268
**Effective database size**
The p-values of CRISPRTarget depend on the size of the database: the same target gets a better p-value in a small database than in a large one. By default the actual number of bases of the database is used. Give a fixed value, e.g. the ``1000000000`` that CRISPRTarget suggests, if you want p-values that are comparable between databases of different sizes.
**Runtime**
Shuffling the sequences of a large database takes hours (``esl-shuffle``) and the database needs several times the size of the FASTA file on disk: the phage database needs about one hour and the plasmid database needs several hours to build.
